one_liner: Executive assistant-plus-analyst for the Navy's Fleet & Family Readiness SES Director: runs the calendar, correspondence, Congressional taskers, and management studies.
fit_summary: Daniel's coordination and meeting-minutes work (a travel company's weekly meetings, mpox response meetings, on-site support to project managers) fits the briefing and action-coordination side. The posting requires five or more years of progressively responsible experience analyzing administrative operations and coordinating executive-level actions for a senior leader; his seven years at IEM are progressive (three titles) but support-level, so document the years and the executive-facing tasks clearly.
eligibility: Open to the public; this is a Nonappropriated Fund (NAF) NF-5 position, not a General Schedule (GS) job, so no federal status is needed.

Requires 5+ years of progressively responsible specialized experience analyzing administrative operations and coordinating executive-level actions for an SES member, flag officer, or equivalent corporate executive.
Requires Secret clearance eligibility; expect a background investigation.
On-site at Washington Navy Yard; no telework or remote work.
strategy: Before writing anything, count your years of executive-support and operations-analysis work. If the total is under five years, this posting is likely out of reach, so look at lower NF or GS-9/11 analyst roles instead.

Frame your IEM work around concrete analysis for government clients, such as after-action reviews, preparedness plans, process assessments, or data collection across jurisdictions, but only where those are accurate.
Spell out any direct support you gave a senior executive or a client official, including scheduling, briefing prep, correspondence, and taskers.
Use your policy expertise as an asset for researching legislative impact and handling Congressional inquiries, and tie it to specific examples.
Keep the resume to two pages, listing dates, hours per week, and the specialized-experience wording for each role.
The window is short (Oct 30–Nov 9, 2026), so have your resume ready before the posting opens and submit early.
resume_bullets: Booked flights for corporate-level staff and answered travel-expense questions in Certify (2019–2024).
Took minutes at a large travel company's weekly meetings (Feb – Aug 2024).
Helped sequence onboarding for FEMA Public Assistance employees by organizing spreadsheets and analyzing the data for decision makers (2019–2020).
interview_questions: Describe a time you managed a senior leader's competing priorities under tight deadlines.
How would you route and respond to a sensitive Congressional inquiry?
Walk us through a management study or process review you led and the recommendations you made.
How do you handle an uncooperative stakeholder whose input you need for a tasker?
watch_outs: The five-year senior-leader experience requirement is the main barrier, and the posting mentions no lower-level substitute.
The role requires a Secret clearance, so expect background investigation delays and be fully candid on the SF-86.
This is fully on-site at the Navy Yard, which means a daily commute from Manassas and no telework.
The posting lists no promotion potential, and the role is heavy on administrative and front-office duties.
